exercise-energy-expenditure.short: The energy a training session costs on top of what you would have burned resting in that time. It is the part subtracted in the energy availability sum.

energy-balance.short: Energy eaten minus all energy spent in a day (resting, digesting, training, moving about). Negative balance means losing body mass, positive means gaining.

problematic-lea.short: Low energy availability that lasts long enough or goes deep enough to harm health or performance: the kind that leads to REDs.

adaptable-lea.short: A short, mild spell of low energy availability (a hard camp, a few days' cut) that the body copes with and fully recovers from once eating matches training again.

oestrogen.short: The main female sex hormone (mostly oestradiol), made by the ovaries when LH and FSH drive them. Besides the menstrual cycle, it keeps bone strong. Men have small amounts.

triiodothyronine.short: The active thyroid hormone. It sets how fast the body's cells burn energy at rest. Low T3 is a sign the body is saving energy.

igf-1.short: A hormone made mainly by the liver when growth hormone signals it. It drives growth and repair of muscle and bone. It falls when energy is short.

leptin.short: A hormone released by fat tissue. Its level tells the brain how much energy the body has in store; it drops quickly when intake falls short.

functional-hypothalamic-amenorrhoea.short: Missing periods because the brain (hypothalamus) has turned down the signals to the ovaries, usually from too little energy or stress, not from disease. It can be reversed.

reds-cat2.short: The IOC's 2023 clinical tool for REDs: screen, rate the signs found by how strong and serious they are, then a doctor makes the diagnosis and plan.

leaf-q.short: Low Energy Availability in Females Questionnaire: 25 questions on injuries, gut and periods that flag female athletes at risk of low energy availability. A screen, not a diagnosis.

sensitivity.short: Of the people who truly have a condition, the share the test flags. 78% sensitivity means it misses 22 in 100 true cases.

specificity.short: Of the people who truly don't have a condition, the share the test correctly clears. 90% specificity means 10 in 100 healthy people are wrongly flagged.

rmr-ratio.short: Measured resting energy use (resting metabolic rate, from a metabolic cart) divided by the value an equation predicts for your size. Below about 0.9 hints the body is saving energy.

disordered-eating.short: Eating behaviour that drifts away from healthy, such as skipping meals, strict food rules or compensating for food with exercise, without meeting the criteria for an eating disorder.

eating-disorder.short: A diagnosed mental illness, such as anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa, in which eating and thoughts about food and body seriously harm health. It needs professional treatment.
